solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: About to grasp what listeners go through

indicators.note: to grasp something is to hold it inside, so the first piece wraps around what follows

blocks.note: re means about or concerning, as in a memo heading
eh? is what you say when you did not catch something
ears are the organs we listen with

explanation.surface: Someone is about to understand what an audience experiences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What listeners go through' looks like one phrase, but only 'go through' is the definition; 'what' is the puzzled interjection.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through a play or speech is to practise it before performing, which is exactly what rehearsing means.

clue.text: Am prone to abuse: I take it all back!

indicators.note: abusing the words mistreats them, mangling their letters into a new order

blocks.note: these seven letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone admits a tendency to rant, then retracts everything they said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I take it all back' sounds like an apology, but here it is someone repossessing goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A repo man repossesses cars and goods from people who have defaulted on their payments.

clue.text: Some pressure to pursue title that’s held by cyclist

blocks.note: a handle is a name or title
a bar is a unit of pressure

explanation.surface: A racing cyclist under pressure while chasing a championship title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To pursue' puts the pressure word after the title word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclist grips the bar at the front of the bike to steer, so it is the thing held.

clue.text: Leading one has to get the record

blocks.note: arch means chief or leading, as in archbishop
one has becomes I've, I have, with I for one

explanation.surface: A front-runner needs to set a new record.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a stored collection of documents, a historical record kept for reference.

clue.text: Habit of minister when talking something over

indicators.note: when talking means the word is judged by its pronunciation, not its spelling

blocks.note: a surplice is the white vestment worn by clergy

explanation.surface: A vicar's habit of going over the same topic in sermons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' looks like a tendency, but it is a garment, as in a monk's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A surplus is an amount left over beyond what is needed, an excess remaining.

clue.text: Like newsprint to be profitable, protecting salesperson’s turnover

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so one piece goes round another
a turnover flips something round, so the salesperson's word is read backwards

blocks.note: a business that pays is profitable
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A newspaper making money by keeping its sales staff's turnover in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover' sounds like staff turnover in business, but here it only flips the salesperson word.
explanation.definitionFit: Newsprint is cheap thin paper, so something resembling it in texture is described as papery.

clue.text: After experiences, twelve on vacation with expedition

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so only the outer letters of the word stay

blocks.note: post is Latin for after, as in postwar
to have an experience is to have it, so experiences means has
twelve emptied of its middle keeps its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A group of twelve back from holiday sharing travel tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expedition' suggests an adventurous trip, but in the definition it means speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste means with great speed, and expedition is an old word for promptness or speed.

clue.text: Old man consuming wine drink recalled something spicy

indicators.note: consuming something takes it inside, so one word swallows the other
recalled is read as called back, so the wine drink comes the other way round

blocks.note: papa is a familiar word for father
kir is white wine with blackcurrant liqueur

explanation.surface: Grandpa remembers a fiery drink he once downed.
explanation.definitionFit: Paprika is a powdered red-pepper spice, used to give heat and colour to dishes like goulash.

clue.text: Theatre permitted audience finally full

indicators.note: finally takes only the closing letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: rep is repertory theatre
let means allowed
the last letter of audience

explanation.surface: A theatre allowed in a crowd and was finally sold out.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete means well filled or sated, as after a large meal.

clue.text: Plant shop has alarm at the front

indicators.note: being at the front means coming first, so the word for alarm leads the answer

blocks.note: panic is sudden alarm; 'at the front' puts it first
in British slang to shop or grass someone is to inform on them to the police

explanation.surface: A shop with an alarm fitted by its front door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shop' looks like a store, but it is the verb meaning to inform on someone, and 'at the front' tells you the alarm word comes before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic grass is a real grass species, genus Panicum, and grasses are plants.

clue.text: Intermediate stage completed after being put back a year

indicators.note: putting something back here means turning it round, so the word for completed is read from the end

blocks.note: time is up when it is completed
p.a. is per annum, a year

explanation.surface: A project delayed by a year finally reaches its halfway point.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupa is the insect stage between larva and adult, in the middle of metamorphosis.

clue.text: Compile hit clue for cracking sort of quiz!

indicators.note: cracking the clue words breaks them apart so they can be rebuilt in a fresh order

blocks.note: all fourteen letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A quizmaster putting together a smash-hit question for contestants to crack.
explanation.definitionFit: A multiple-choice quiz offers several possible responses to each question and the contestant picks one.

clue.text: Those who catch rabbits, heading off after November

indicators.note: with its heading off a word loses its first letter

blocks.note: November is N in the NATO phonetic alphabet
in British slang to rabbit is to chatter on, to jabber

explanation.surface: Hunters who catch rabbits set out after November.
explanation.walkthrough: Rabbits look like the animals being caught, but the word is the slang verb for talking endlessly. JABBERS loses its J, and N goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To nab is informal for to seize or arrest, so nabbers are people who catch others.

clue.text: Small set of wheels carried on a cycle

blocks.note: a newspaper that carried a story ran it; the past participle is run
taken as written
a round is a cycle of events, as in a round of talks

explanation.surface: A tiny wheeled toy transported on a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set of wheels' is slang for a car, and a runaround is the British word for a small car used for short trips.
explanation.definitionFit: A runaround is a small, cheap car for local errands, and wheels is slang for a car.

clue.text: Expressed frustration as small, hard blocks carelessly handled

indicators.note: something that blocks a passage sits inside it, so these letters go inside the other piece

blocks.note: to paw something is to handle it clumsily
S is the standard abbreviation for small
H for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone gets annoyed watching small, hard toy blocks being knocked about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blocks' reads like children's building blocks, but it is the verb: S and H block the middle of PAWED.
explanation.definitionFit: Pshaw is an old exclamation of contempt or impatience, so to have pshawed is to have voiced annoyance.

clue.text: Sport, one a few find boring

blocks.note: to sport clothes is to wear them
I is the Roman numeral one
some means a few

explanation.surface: A sport that only a handful of people find dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' looks like a game, but it is the verb meaning to wear proudly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wearisome is tedious and tiring, the same quality as being boring.

clue.text: One often powered by stream that’s turned dry in June, finally

indicators.note: something turned is facing the other way, so the word for dry is read backwards
finally points to the last letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: brut describes very dry champagne
taken as written
the last letter of June

explanation.surface: A summer stream has run dry, stranding whatever relies on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry in June' paints a drought, but dry is the champagne word BRUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbine is a machine whose blades are spun by moving water or steam, and many are driven by a flowing current.

clue.text: Endless Burgundy in green bottles

indicators.note: bottles here is a verb: the words hold something inside them, as a bottle holds wine

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of Burgundy, the word in and the start of green

explanation.surface: An unlimited supply of Burgundy wine in green glass bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottles' reads as a noun for the wine, but it is the verb that holds the answer inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something undying never stops or fades away, so it has no end.

clue.text: Was revealing, like the costume one ordered?

blocks.note: first meaning: the past tense of bespeak, to indicate or show, a rather old-fashioned usage
second meaning: made to a customer's order, as a tailored suit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Revealing' next to 'costume' suggests a skimpy outfit, but the first half is an old verb meaning indicated.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the archaic past tense of a verb meaning to show and an adjective for made-to-measure clothing.

clue.text: Our team in the old days, when time, making transmission

blocks.note: our team is us, we
BC, before Christ, labels ancient dates
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A fan recalls their team's glory days while watching an old broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A webcast is a broadcast sent out over the internet, so it is a kind of transmission.

clue.text: Little one quiet and rather pale

blocks.note: a whit is a tiny amount, as in 'not a whit'
I is the Roman numeral one
sh! is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A small child who is silent and looks a bit washed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little one' reads as a child, but the two words give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitish means somewhat white, a light colour that is fairly pale.

clue.text: Old railway porter’s maybe succeeded in freeing chest?

blocks.note: BR was British Rail, the former national railway
porter is a dark beer, an example of ale, so porter's becomes ALE'S
S is the abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: An old railway porter freeing a trunk from a luggage van.
explanation.walkthrough: The railway porter carrying a chest is the surface picture; porter is the beer and the chest is a bust.
explanation.definitionFit: Going braless means not wearing a bra, which frees the bust from support.

clue.text: Drew, possibly accompanying note, something taken from letter

blocks.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
Nancy Drew is the girl detective of the mystery novels

explanation.surface: An artist drew something to go with a note taken from a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: A letter here is someone who lets property, a landlord, not a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenancy is the right to occupy property that a tenant takes from the landlord who lets it.

clue.text: Bigotry perhaps that’s not tasteless?

definitions.note: adjectival phrase for a noun answer: discrimination is the quality of not being tasteless

blocks.note: first meaning: unfair treatment of people because of prejudice, of which bigotry is one form
second meaning: refined judgement, the ability to tell good from bad

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'not tasteless' is a playful way of describing good taste.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both prejudiced unequal treatment and the fine judgement of a connoisseur with good taste.

clue.text: Carry off old drunk?

blocks.note: to carry off a prize is to win it
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to haul away an old man who is drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A wino is a habitual drinker of cheap wine, informally a drunk.

clue.text: Sort of cake you quietly consume after eleven?

indicators.note: after sends the word for consume to the end, behind the word for eleven

blocks.note: U is text-speak for you
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
a football or cricket side has eleven players
to down food or drink is to consume it

explanation.surface: Discreetly eating cake at elevenses, the British mid-morning snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After eleven' suggests the time of day, but eleven is a team, as a football or cricket side has eleven players.
explanation.definitionFit: An upside-down cake is baked with fruit at the bottom of the tin and then turned out the other way up.

clue.text: As one at first approaches, fancy going over the top?

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the following word is used

blocks.note: the first letter of approaches
a whimsical definition: wanting things to excess

explanation.surface: A soldier advances while imagining charging out of the trench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going over the top' evokes troops leaving the trenches, but here it means excessive, so fancy that is excessive is greed.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are agreed hold the same opinion, so they act or think as one.

clue.text: A large scythe has been mislaid, so live without it

indicators.note: something mislaid is put in the wrong place, so these letters end up out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmer has lost the big scythe and must manage without it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' in the definition is the familiar euphemism for sex, not the scythe the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To live chastely is to abstain from sexual relations, and 'it' is a coy slang word for sex.
